rationale: Repeated groups showed no reproducible marginal bias after a tree, but one interaction had nonzero residual variance. A group could prefer one situation and dislike another, producing little overall bias. Test whether several groups share a small number of such response patterns.
model: Use the previously sealed out-of-group original-tree log odds as an offset for each of the 4061 fitting rows. Infer recurring profiles and varying field keys without names. Define context effects from one-hot variable fields and the joint context. Initialize latent profiles with a fixed-seed KMeans on shrunk context residuals. Fit a two- or four-class shared-group latent response model for 14 expectation-maximization rounds. Jointly optimize the class-specific ridge logistic corrections, with centered offsets, regularization 24, posterior temperature .75 and smoothed group proportions. Known query profiles use their train-only posterior; unseen profiles use the global prior. The ordinary frozen tree supplies the starting probability on query rows. Count both whole model fits, the two initializations, and each joint M-step optimizer separately.
evaluation: Freeze both model outputs on all three development panels, elect against the strong research pair on the 808-row nomination, then require nonnegative on 817 and 807 with pooled +.003 before considering ordinary validation. Show the predeclared standalone differences from the teammate's original tree, using exactly the same approach as the previous residual study. No external or course validation, test or model API.
